title: Cardiovascular High-Yield Flashcards
lede: Test your knowledge on board-relevant cardiovascular pathophysiology, pharmacology, clinical triads, and physical exam findings.

cards.front: What is the classic clinical triad of Severe Aortic Stenosis?
cards.back:
SAD: Syncope, Angina, Dyspnea.

Key finding: Crescendo-decrescendo systolic ejection murmur at RUSB radiating to the carotids with pulsus parvus et tardus.

cards.front: How do GLP-1 and Dual GLP-1/GIP agonists impact cardiovascular outcomes?
cards.back: They reduce Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE), lower systemic vascular resistance, promote weight loss, and aid in favorable cardiac remodeling.

cards.front: What four major factors determine Myocardial Oxygen Consumption (MVO₂)?
cards.back:
1. Heart Rate
2. Wall Tension (Preload & Radius)
3. Afterload (Arterial Pressure)
4. Inotropy (Contractility)

cards.front: What are the four anatomic features of Tetralogy of Fallot?
cards.back:
PROVe:
1. P - Pulmonary infundibular stenosis
2. R - Right ventricular hypertrophy
3. O - Overriding aorta
4. V - Ventricular septal defect (VSD)
